req.title: Session cookie has HttpOnly attribute
req.statement: The system shall set HttpOnly on the session cookie.

doc.reasoning: The requirement mandates that the session cookie carries the HttpOnly attribute. To test this we must trigger session-cookie issuance (via POST /auth/login with valid credentials), then inspect the Set-Cookie response header. Three angles are needed: (1) positive – valid login produces a session cookie with HttpOnly; (2) negative – a request that never creates a session (GET /auth/login) must NOT produce a session cookie with HttpOnly, confirming the attribute is tied to session creation; (3) boundary – the HttpOnly flag must appear as a discrete token in the header, not merely as a substring of another attribute name, catching mutations that change 'HttpOnly' to 'httponly', remove it, or replace it with a different flag.

tests.name: test_session_cookie_has_httponly_on_successful_login
preconditions: App is created with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
Database contains user id=1 username='test' password='test'
POST /auth/login is submitted with correct credentials
actions: Create in-process Flask app with test config
Inspect the Set-Cookie header of the response
expected: The cookie named 'session' contains the HttpOnly attribute
trace: R-FLASKR-043: session cookie shall have HttpOnly attribute
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_session_cookie_has_httponly_on_successful_login():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    set_cookie = r.headers.get('Set-Cookie', '')
    assert set_cookie != '', 'Set-Cookie header must be present after login'
    cookie_attrs = [attr.strip() for attr in set_cookie.split(';')]
    httponly_flags = [a for a in cookie_attrs if a.lower() == 'httponly']
    assert len(httponly_flags) == 1, f'Expected exactly one HttpOnly token, got: {cookie_attrs}'

test_session_cookie_has_httponly_on_successful_login()

tests.name: test_httponly_token_is_exact_and_standalone
preconditions: App is created with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
Database contains user id=1 username='test' password='test'
POST /auth/login is submitted with correct credentials
actions: Create in-process Flask app with test config
Assert that exactly one token equals 'HttpOnly' (case-sensitive) and that no token merely contains 'HttpOnly' as a substring of a longer word
expected: Exactly one semicolon-delimited token in Set-Cookie equals 'HttpOnly' (case-sensitive)
No token is a superset string like 'HttpOnlyExtra' or 'NotHttpOnly'
trace: R-FLASKR-043: HttpOnly attribute must appear as a discrete, correctly-cased token
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_httponly_token_is_exact_and_standalone():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    set_cookie = r.headers.get('Set-Cookie', '')
    assert set_cookie != '', 'Set-Cookie header must be present'
    tokens = [t.strip() for t in set_cookie.split(';')]
    exact_matches = [t for t in tokens if t == 'HttpOnly']
    assert len(exact_matches) == 1, (
        f'Expected exactly 1 token equal to "HttpOnly", found {exact_matches} in {tokens}'
    )
    superset_matches = [t for t in tokens if 'HttpOnly' in t and t != 'HttpOnly']
    assert len(superset_matches) == 0, (
        f'HttpOnly appears embedded in another token: {superset_matches}'
    )

test_httponly_token_is_exact_and_standalone()

tests.name: test_session_cookie_httponly_after_failed_login_attempt
preconditions: App is created with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
Database contains user id=1 username='test' password='test'
POST /auth/login is submitted with wrong password
actions: Create in-process Flask app with test config
Inspect response status and Set-Cookie header
expected: Response status code is 200 (login page re-rendered, not redirected)
If a Set-Cookie header is present it must still carry HttpOnly (Flask may set a session cookie for flash messages)
No session cookie without HttpOnly is emitted
trace: R-FLASKR-043: HttpOnly must be set on any session cookie regardless of login outcome

from flaskr import create_app

def test_session_cookie_httponly_present_after_logout_redirect():

    client = app.test_client()

    logout_r = client.get('/auth/logout')

    set_cookie = logout_r.headers.get('Set-Cookie', '')
    if set_cookie:
        tokens = [t.strip() for t in set_cookie.split(';')]
        httponly_flags = [t for t in tokens if t.lower() == 'httponly']
        assert len(httponly_flags) >= 1, (
            f'Session cookie on logout missing HttpOnly: {tokens}'
        )
